After a container is running there is no way to modify its configuration without manually stopping, removing, and re-creating it. This adds a single-form Edit workflow that handles that lifecycle automatically.

## Backend

- **`POST /update-container`** — new `UpdateContainer` handler: inspects the target container, stops it if running, removes it, pulls/resolves the image if needed, recreates with the new spec, and starts it; returns the new container ID
- **`ContainerDetail.Command`** — new field populated from Podman Inspect `Config.Cmd`
- All 7 Podman operations are wired through mockable package-level vars (`updateContainerConnection`, `updateContainerInspect`, `updateContainerStop`, `updateContainerRemove`, `updateContainerEnsureImage`, `updateContainerCreateWithSpec`, `updateContainerStart`) for testability

```go
// POST /update-container
type UpdateContainerRequest struct {
    ContainerID   string   `json:"containerId"`
    Image         string   `json:"image"`
    Name          string   `json:"name,omitempty"`
    Ports         []string `json:"ports,omitempty"`
    Env           []string `json:"env,omitempty"`
    Volumes       []string `json:"volumes,omitempty"`
    RestartPolicy string   `json:"restartPolicy,omitempty"`
    AutoRemove    bool     `json:"autoRemove,omitempty"`
    Command       string   `json:"command,omitempty"`
}
```

- 12 new unit tests covering all validation paths and the full stop → remove → recreate → start flow with mocked Podman operations

## Frontend

- New **Edit** tab on the container detail page between Overview and Logs
- All fields pre-populated from the live container state: image, name, command, ports (parsed from `8080:80/tcp`), env vars (`KEY=VALUE`), volume binds (`hostPath:containerPath:Z`), restart policy, auto-remove
- On save: calls `POST /update-container` and navigates to the new container's detail page (ID changes on recreate)
- Auto Remove toggle is disabled when a restart policy other than `no` is selected

## Summary

Adds [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — a static analysis tool for GitHub Actions workflow security — to the CI pipeline.

## What's included

### `.github/workflows/zizmor.yml`
- **Non-blocking** integration using SARIF upload to GitHub Code Scanning
- Runs on PRs and pushes to `main` when workflow files change
- Daily scheduled scan (06:30 UTC) to catch drift
- Uses the official [`zizmorcore/zizmor-action`](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-action) (pinned to SHA)
- Results appear in the **Security → Code Scanning** tab and as PR annotations

### `.github/zizmor.yml`
- Configuration file that suppresses `dangerous-triggers` findings on 4 workflows that intentionally use `workflow_run`/`pull_request_target` with explicit fork validation guards

## Baseline scan

The initial scan found **236 findings** (after suppression) across 33 of 39 workflows:

| Severity | Rule | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| error | template-injection | 83 | Mostly `inputs.*`, `env.*`, `matrix.*` in `run:` — not externally controllable |
| warning | template-injection | 40 | Same pattern |
| warning | artipacked | 39 | Missing `persist-credentials: false` — auto-fixable |
| warning | excessive-permissions | 28 | Intentional write permissions for PR comments, checks, etc. |
| note | template-injection | 38 | Low confidence |
| error | excessive-permissions | 8 | Workflow-level write perms on backport/release workflows |

These findings are informational and do **not** block CI. They'll be visible in the Security tab for gradual triage and improvement.

## References
- [zizmor docs](https://docs.zizmor.sh/)
- [microsoft/linux-package-repositories](https://github.com/microsoft/linux-package-repositories/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml) — similar integration in another Microsoft repo
- [dotnet/maui](https://github.com/dotnet/maui) — uses inline zizmor ignore comments

This PR loosens the restriction on where OpenTelemetry and sentry can be loaded to more than just the web application servers. Originally, it was restricted to test Sentry's impact to the web apps for demonstration purposes. Now that we have enabled Sentry on the servers, we can now use it for error collection in cron and active jobs.

To prevent OpenTelemetry and sentry from activating in unit tests, the `UNIT_TEST` env var (which is set by test_helper) is used.

Additionally, previously OTel produces initialization logs which were noisy. However, those have since been removed by the otel log level.

https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/TINKERPOP-3233
This is the first part of resolving the ticket.

This change fixes a bug in Go in which characters that should be escaped are being replaced by a dot.
Bug:
The traversal `result, err := g.V().Has(vertexLabel, "name", "m   m").Next()` would generate the GremlinLang `g.V().has(vertexLabel, "name", "m.m").next()`.
New behaviour:
The traversal `result, err := g.V().Has(vertexLabel, "name", "m   m").Next()` would generate the GremlinLang `g.V().has(vertexLabel, "name", "m\tm").next()`.

A test has been added to `gremlinlang_test.go` for testing all cases that should be escaped.

- 4 THEORETICAL findings (plausible but unconfirmed)

- Symlink checks present and consistent across file reads

- No hardcoded secrets found

body:
## Summary
- Adds a new `Anomaly` / `Inconclusive` / `Low` finding for TLS SNI hostnames that are valid UTF-8 but contain non-ASCII codepoints (e.g. raw U-labels like `"café.example"`, `"пример.example"`, `"🦀.example"`). RFC 6066 §3 requires `HostName` to be ASCII, with internationalized names sent as A-labels per RFC 5890 (`xn--…` Punycode form). Closes #51.
- Renames `SniValue::Utf8(String)` → `SniValue::Ascii(String)` (the old name was misleading — ASCII is also valid UTF-8) and adds a new `NonAsciiUtf8 { hostname, hex }` variant. The existing `NonUtf8` variant is unchanged.
- Flips the pin-test from #50 (`test_valid_utf8_non_ascii_sni_currently_not_flagged` → `test_valid_utf8_non_ascii_sni_emits_finding`) and adds 3 new positive cases (Cyrillic, emoji, Punycode regression).
- Code review (`code-reviewer`) applied pre-merge: zero critical, zero important, all suggestions explicit defers.
- Follow-up #54 filed for the related ASCII-control-code gap (S1 — pre-existing, out of #51's scope).

## Real-world false-positive risk
Validated with Perplexity that all major TLS clients auto-Punycode internationalized hostnames before sending the SNI:

| Client | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **rustls** | Rejects raw UTF-8 at the `ServerName` API level, requires Punycode upfront |
| **Chrome / BoringSSL** | Always Punycode (per RFC 3492 + 6066) |
| **Firefox / NSS** | Always Punycode (URL bar may display Unicode for user-friendliness, but the wire is always Punycode) |
| **curl / libcurl** | Auto-converts via libidn2 before calling OpenSSL |
| **OpenSSL raw API** | Passes verbatim — but expects ASCII from the caller; only legitimate path to a raw U-label SNI is a custom application using OpenSSL directly without IDNA prep |

So the false-positive surface is small: a buggy custom client, an OpenSSL-direct app that forgot to Punycode, or an attacker tool. Severity is `Anomaly` / `Inconclusive` / `Low` — same rationale as the non-UTF-8 finding from #49.

## Implementation
```rust
enum SniValue {
    Ascii(String),                                  // RFC compliant
    NonAsciiUtf8 { hostname: String, hex: String }, // valid UTF-8, non-ASCII (NEW)
    NonUtf8 { lossy: String, hex: String },         // invalid UTF-8 (existing)
}
```

`extract_sni` uses `s.is_ascii()` to split the UTF-8 case. `handle_client_hello` uses an exhaustive `match` on the variants, so a future variant addition (e.g. for #54's ASCII-control-code case) will fail to compile until handled. Map-keying for `NonAsciiUtf8` is the bare hostname (no `<non-ascii:HEX>` tagging needed — valid UTF-8 strings have no collision risk because `from_utf8` is a bijection on well-formed bytes).

## Findings shape
The new finding mirrors the existing `NonUtf8` finding pattern for consistency:
- `category: Anomaly`, `verdict: Inconclusive`, `confidence: Low`
- Summary: `"TLS SNI contains non-ASCII characters (RFC 6066 requires A-labels per RFC 5890): {hostname:?}"` — `{:?}` Debug formatter to escape any control codepoints that might survive UTF-8 decoding (e.g. U+0085 NEL)
- Evidence: `vec![format!("hex: {hex}")]` for forensic byte-level review
- `mitre_technique: None` (matches existing TLS findings; no clean ATT&CK technique for protocol-format violations)

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --test tls_analyzer_tests` — 21/21 pass (~650ms; was 18 before)
- [x] `cargo test` — full suite green
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] Code review pass (`code-reviewer`): zero critical, zero important; one defer-only suggestion (S1 — ASCII control codes) filed as #54
- [x] Real-world false-positive risk Perplexity-validated against rustls, OpenSSL, Chrome/BoringSSL, Firefox/NSS, curl/libcurl
- [x] RFC 6066 §3 ASCII requirement and RFC 5890 A-label requirement reconfirmed (already validated earlier this session via direct RFC fetch)

## New tests
1. **test_valid_utf8_non_ascii_sni_emits_finding** (flipped from #50's pin-test) — `"café.example"`, asserts category/verdict/confidence/RFC mention/A-label mention/hex evidence (`636166c3a92e6578616d706c65`).
2. **test_cyrillic_sni_emits_non_ascii_finding** — `"пример.example"` (Cyrillic 2-byte UTF-8 sequences).
3. **test_emoji_sni_emits_non_ascii_finding** — `"🦀.example"` (4-byte UTF-8 codepoint).
4. **test_punycode_a_label_does_not_emit_non_ascii_finding** — `"xn--caf-dma.example"` regression: the RFC-compliant Punycode form is pure ASCII and must NOT be flagged.

Appearance cosmetics (hair, eyes, facial hair) were drawn using only their own `ax/ay/sx/sy` layer xforms, ignoring `HEAD_XFORM`. Since these cosmetics are authored relative to the head bone, their effective transform must be composed with `HEAD_XFORM`.

## Changes

- **`composeXform(base, child)`** — new helper that composes two xforms: additive offsets (`ax/ay`) and multiplicative scales (`sx/sy`), with safe defaults (`0` / `1`)
- **`renderProfile()`** — back and front cosmetic `drawLayer` calls now use `composeXform(HEAD_XFORM, layer)`; head base and untinted overlay continue using `HEAD_XFORM` directly
- **`buildRenderChain()`** — diagnostic transform entries for cosmetics also use the composed value, so copied diagnostics reflect what is actually rendered

```js
// Appearance cosmetics are authored relative to the head bone,
// so their effective transform is composed with HEAD_XFORM.
function composeXform(base, child) {
  return {
    ax: (base.ax ?? 0) + (child.ax ?? 0),
    ay: (base.ay ?? 0) + (child.ay ?? 0),
    sx: (base.sx ?? 1) * (child.sx ?? 1),
    sy: (base.sy ?? 1) * (child.sy ?? 1),
  };
}

// Before
drawLayer(ctx, img, layer, filter);
// After
drawLayer(ctx, img, composeXform(HEAD_XFORM, layer), filter);
```

Implement proper xform composition in the standalone portrait picker so that appearance cosmetics inherit the head sprite’s base xform.

2) Composition semantics:
   - ax/ay are offsets in bone-length units: effectiveAx = HEAD_XFORM.ax + layer.ax; effectiveAy = HEAD_XFORM.ay + layer.ay
   - sx/sy are scales: effectiveSx = HEAD_XFORM.sx * layer.sx; effectiveSy = HEAD_XFORM.sy * layer.sy

User: Is there something scaling and offsetting the head sprites that isnt affecting the hair, beard and other cosmetic sprites?

Assistant: Yes. In your render path there’s a **per-bone style transform (“xform”) being applied to the HEAD sprite via the fighter’s `spriteStyle`**, and that transform **doesn’t automatically apply to hair/beard cosmetics unless those cosmetic layers are also being drawn with the same `styleKey` / xform key**.

### Where the head scaling/offset comes from
In `docs/js/sprites.js`, every draw call can get a `styleOverride.xform` composed from:

1) the fighter’s base `style.xform` (from config / sprite style), and  
2) any runtime animation xform overrides (`GAME.ANIM_STYLE_OVERRIDES[entity.id]`), merged via `composeStyleXformEntry`.

That logic is here: `composeStyleOverrides(styleKey, baseOptions)` and `applyAnimOptions(styleKey, baseOptions)` in `sprites.js` (around the snippet you saw). citeturn1search5

So if your config has something like an xform entry for `"head"` (or whatever the styleKey resolves to for the head sprite), it will scale/offset the head sprite.

### Why hair/beard cosmetics might *not* follow it
Cosmetics are drawn as additional layers, but the **xform that gets applied depends on the `styleKey` used for that particular draw**.

If hair/beard cosmetics are:
- attached to the **head bone** but drawn using a **different styleKey** (or a different normalized key),
- or treated as “appearance layers” with their own `styleKey`/slot style key,
- or drawn with options that don’t run through `applyAnimOptions(styleKey, ...)` with the head styleKey,

…then they won’t pick up the head’s `style.xform` entry even though they visually “belong” to the head.

In other words: the xform is not “bone-global”; it’s “styleKey/global-per-part draw”.

2) In `sprites.js`, find where the **head sprite is drawn** and note the `styleKey` passed into `applyAnimOptions(...)`, then find where **hair/beard layers are drawn** and compare which `styleKey` they use.

body:
## Summary

Borrows [tobi/qmd](https://github.com/tobi/qmd)'s folder-context pattern. Adds an optional `_context.md` file per wiki folder describing what lives there and which queries should traverse it — so `/wiki-query` can skip irrelevant folders instead of reading random pages to infer their purpose. Saves context tokens on every deep query.

Closes #60

## What

### New module `llmwiki/context_md.py` (stdlib-only)

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `is_context_file(path)` | Exact-name guard used by `discover_sources()` to skip these files |
| `load_folder_context(folder)` | Reads `<folder>/_context.md`, parses minimal key/value frontmatter, returns `(meta, body)` or `None` |
| `folder_context_summary(body)` | Extracts the first non-heading paragraph, collapses whitespace, truncates at `max_chars` — used as a tooltip/header |
| `find_uncontexted_folders(root, threshold=10)` | Lint walker that yields `(folder, page_count)` for any folder with >threshold pages but no `_context.md`, skipping hidden dirs and not counting `_context.md` itself |
| `collect_folder_contexts(root)` | Bulk loader — returns `{folder: (meta, body)}` for every `_context.md` under `root` |

### Build integration
`llmwiki/build.py`'s `discover_sources()` now skips `_context.md` so these files never pollute the session index, search index, or AI-consumable exports. The real build still emits 679 HTML files — the new files are metadata-only.

### CLAUDE.md updates
- **Query Workflow** step 2: before walking into a folder, read its `_context.md` if one exists and use the summary to decide whether to descend
- **Lint Workflow** step 7: warn on uncontexted folders >10 files, with a ready-to-run snippet

### Seeded stubs
Three `_context.md` files under `wiki/` to bootstrap the pattern:

- **`wiki/entities/_context.md`** — "People, companies, projects, products, tools. Walk this for who/what-product/which-company queries. Skip for idea/pattern queries (prefer concepts/)."
- **`wiki/concepts/_context.md`** — "Ideas, patterns, methods, decisions. Walk this for how/why/trade-off queries. Skip for specific-entity queries (prefer entities/)."

body:
… type errors

*   **What:** Replaced vulnerable `innerHTML` assignment with `DOMParser` when adding jdenticon SVGs to the DOM in `client/src/ui.ts`. Also hex-encodes the `senderId` before passing it to `jdenticon.toSvg` to guarantee the seed is strictly alphanumeric. Added missing test dependencies (`happy-dom`, `@happy-dom/global-registrator`) to `client/package.json`.
*   **Risk:** An attacker could potentially inject malicious scripts via a crafted `senderId` (Cross-Site Scripting), leading to session hijacking. Missing devDependencies caused `tsc` type-checking to fail on deploy.
*   **Solution:** Hex-encoding the input seed ensures it cannot contain any HTML entities or attributes. Appending the generated SVG securely via `DOMParser` instead of `innerHTML` prevents any possibility of code execution during DOM parsing. Included `happy-dom` dependencies in `package.json` for proper VPS deployments.
